hints.title: Stream Tokenization and Ranking
hints.text: Input text contains varying whitespace separating terms across lines. How can an arbitrary text stream be split into individual words, counted, and ordered by occurrence in descending order?

hints.title: Pipelined Word Aggregation
hints.text: Standard command-line utilities can transform whitespace into line breaks, aggregate duplicate adjacent tokens to count frequencies, and sort numerically.

hints.title: Pipelined Unix Text Processing
hints.text: Read words.txt and translate spaces into newlines using tr -s. Filter blank lines, sort the tokens alphabetically, count unique occurrences with uniq -c, sort numerically in descending order using sort -nr, and reformat columns to display the word followed by its count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```bash
cat words.txt | tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | awk '{print $2 " " $1}'
```

variables: W: total number of words in words.txt
complexity.notes: Stream pipelining through sort, uniq, and awk format projection.
